tools.name: well_measure_subscriptions
tools.title: Measure subscriptions from bank outflows
tools.description:
Measure the workspace's subscriptions from its bank and credit card outflows: which suppliers it pays on a regular cadence, what each costs per month and per year, and how the spend moved month by month. It draws no card.

Call it when the user asks what they pay for on a regular basis, what their subscriptions cost, or how that spend moved. Then draw the two cards from its result, trend first:
  1. `well_render_category_trend` with one `category_trends` entry, passed as it is.
  2. `well_render_monthly_pivot` with the `pivots` entry of the same currency, passed as it is.
When the result holds more than one currency, draw one pair per currency. Never add two currencies together. When `category_trends` and `pivots` are empty, no subscription was found: say so and draw nothing.

**The server applies every rule, and the result states each one in `rules`.** Quote the figures as returned: never recompute a cost, a total or a cadence, and never loosen a rule to list a supplier the user expects. A supplier in `not_recurring` missed the rule named in its `missed_rule`.

Every amount in the result is in the major units of its currency, never in cents: `1860` is 1,860.00 EUR, not 18.60 EUR.

The window is fixed: the last 24 complete calendar months in UTC and the running month are read, and the cards draw the last 12 complete months (the pivot draws the running month apart, marked as in progress). `window`, `current_month` and `display_months` say which months those were.

**A supplier row is a company or a bank label.** A row with a `company_id` is a company. A row whose `company_id` is null carries a `label_means_id` instead: a payee Well knows only by the label the bank prints, named by `name`, with no domain. List it like any other supplier, under its `name`. Never pass a `label_means_id` where a `company_id` is asked for: no contract, record or company lookup takes it.

What the result is:
  - `subscriptions`: the suppliers on a cadence (monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, yearly) whose category is software or a service paid on a schedule, largest cost per month first, at most 50; `subscription_count` is the full count, and a list that shows fewer says how many it shows. Each carries its cadence evidence, its amount pattern (fixed, changed, varying), the amount its cost per month starts from, the cost per month and per year, its latest month, `possibly_ended`, its category and `state` (possibly_ended, rising, falling, varying, stable): the one section it belongs to. Never list one supplier under two states.
  - `uncategorised_recurring`: suppliers on a cadence whose category says nothing about them (none, residual or suspense), at most 25; `uncategorised_recurring_count` is the full count and `uncategorised_recurring_monthly_total` their cost per month, one entry per currency, as decimal strings, over all of them and not only the listed ones. They are not counted as subscriptions and are in no total: give the count and the monthly total as leads (recurring payments Well cannot categorise yet, which may be subscriptions), and point the user to categorizing their counterparties. Never add the monthly total to `totals`.
  - `totals`: per currency, the subscription count, the total cost per month and per year, and the part from subscriptions flagged as possibly ended (already inside the total).
  - `possible_duplicates`: subscription suppliers charged their own price more than once in a month. A lead to check, never a verdict, and never in a total. Taxes, meals, travel and a one-off transfer are never in it.
  - `not_recurring`: suppliers paid in the window that are not subscriptions, at most 25, with the rule missed (one_month, too_few_months, multiple_debits_in_month, irregular_gaps, not_subscription_category). `not_subscription_category` is a supplier paid on a cadence whose category is work, fees or spend by use, such as an agency or a contractor: never call it a subscription.
  - `unattributed`: outflows whose payee resolves to no company and to no bank label, such as a person or a row with no payee. Real spend with no supplier to repeat, so never on a cadence.
  - `category_trends` and `pivots`: the render inputs, one per currency. A trend holds at most 6 lines, the smallest categories rolled into the last one.
  - `excluded`: what fell out, counted apart. `internal_transfers` are movements between the workspace's own accounts, card repayments among them. A charge on a credit card the workspace connected is measured like a bank debit, on the day of the charge and against its supplier, so its repayment is never counted a second time. `no_asset_movement` counts the outflows with no leg on an owned bank account or credit card: rows whose payer resolved to no account, a charge on a card that is not connected among them. Say so whenever the count is not zero: payments on rows linked to no connected account are NOT measured here. `payments_to_own_accounts` are payments to another owned account, such as a loan, `own_company` payments to the workspace's own company, `unreadable_rows` rows with no readable amount or currency. `category_keys` lists the categories never counted as subscriptions (transfers, treasury, loans, taxes, salaries, social charges), and `category_excluded` is how many bank outflows those categories removed. `internal_transfers` counts a transfer whatever its category. A `null` count was not measured, which is not zero.

**What pays each one.** Each subscription carries `paid_with`: the means that paid its latest debit (`last_paid_on`). `card_last_four` and `card_name` name the card when Well knows it. `card_connector_slug` names the connector that synced that card, such as `qonto`, and `card_workspace_connector_id` names that connection: a card action runs on it, never on another connection. `account_name` names the account debited. `card_last_four: null` means the debit names no card (a transfer, a direct debit, or a bank that does not say), never "no card". `paid_with: null` means the read named no payer; `payers_truncated: true` means the read hit its cap, so some subscriptions carry none. Show a card as its last four digits only, such as ••1234.

**Never claim a saving.** A possibly ended subscription or a possible duplicate is what the bank shows, and Well cannot see whether a service is in use.

**The yearly leads.** Each subscription carries `rise_per_year`: what its price rise costs over a year, null when the amount did not rise. `rise_leads` lists the rises that count as leads: a possibly ended subscription is none, and a copy already counted in `paid_in_several_workspaces` is none, because dropping that copy drops its rise too. `annual_lead_totals` sums, per currency, every rise lead and every extra copy below, with how many it sums. Quote them as returned: a lead to check, never a saving made.

**Every workspace of the person.** When the person asks where they can save or what they could cut, do not answer from this tool alone: load the `subscription-spend` skill (with well_get_skill, or with the host's own skill tool when the Well skills are installed in it) and follow it, because it orders the answer (the subscriptions first, then the leads, every amount per year) and names each workspace. A list ask, such as "which subscriptions do I pay?", loads the skill first too, on an AI app host and on WhatsApp; on WhatsApp it takes that same answer across the person's workspaces. On WhatsApp, pass `workspaces: "all_my_workspaces"` on every call. Elsewhere, pass it when the person asks where they can save, what to cut, or about everything they pay across their workspaces. `other_workspaces` returns the measured other-workspace groups selected for named blocks. On WhatsApp, the tool reads up to 10 other workspaces of the login the turn acts as, the starting login or the one picked with `/account`; elsewhere, it reads up to 10 other real workspaces this same signed-in person is a member of. Each returned group comes with its subscriptions, totals and possible duplicates. `workspace_order.workspace_ids` lists at most 10 groups in answer order, including the current workspace when its group holds something. `workspace_groups_omitted` counts measured groups outside that limit; `other_workspaces_omitted` gives each omitted other workspace's descriptor, subscription count and check facts (possible duplicates and possibly ended subscriptions) so the answer can still name them. A group whose read failed, read partially or truncated keeps a named slot ahead of readable groups, so it is never dropped by the cap. `other_workspaces_skipped` counts other workspaces not read; totals and leads use all workspaces measured, including unnamed groups. `paid_in_several_workspaces` holds the suppliers two or more of them pay for what reads as one subscription: the same payee domain, cadence and category, at a comparable cost. When the person may read more workspaces than that, `other_workspaces_skipped` counts the ones not read, and every total covers the workspaces read only. Well finds those workspaces from the person; a workspace is never named in the call, and an AI app connection reaches only the workspaces its grant covers. `all_workspaces_totals` gives, per currency, the subscription count and the cost per year of every workspace read, this one included. `other_workspaces_status` says why the list is what it is: `not_requested`, `read`, `no_signed_in_person` or `unreadable` (which is not "no other workspace"). The cards draw this workspace only.

**Workspace names and empty groups.** `leads[].targets` and `kept` carry each target's `workspace_name`, including a target in a group omitted from `other_workspaces`. `other_workspaces_empty_count` counts other workspaces that were fully read and had no subscriptions.

**The order and the numbers.** `workspace_order.workspace_ids` is the order to list the workspaces in: the biggest cost per year first, in `workspace_order.currency`, and on a tie this workspace (the one the call runs in), else the person's own space. `leads` is every yearly lead `annual_lead_totals` sums, numbered in the order a reply shows them: the biggest `amount_per_year` first, and on a tie the lead acting in this workspace, else in the person's own space. Each lead carries its `kind` (rise, paid_in_several_workspaces), the one `action` it proposes (renegotiate, cancel_extra_copies) and its `targets`: the workspace and the supplier row each action runs on (a null `workspace_id` is this workspace). A `cancel_extra_copies` lead also names in `kept` the copy it keeps; show the kept copy and the copies cancelled on its line. Show each lead under its `number`, never renumber them: the person answers with these numbers, and the same measure numbers the same leads the same way. `lead_key` joins the action, the supplier, the sorted target workspaces, the sorted target supplier rows and the supplier row of the copy kept: when a person answers a number from an earlier answer, act only when the lead under that number in a fresh measure has the same `lead_key` as in the answer they read, because the figures can move and give the number another supplier, action or workspace.

**Naming a workspace.** `workspace` and each `other_workspaces[].workspace` carry `workspace_name`, `own_company_name`, `is_personal` and `bank_names`. Name a workspace from them, by what sets it apart, never by a generic label such as "personal space" alone.

`partial: true` means nothing was measured: the read was cut short, or the workspace holds no bank account and no credit card. Say so rather than reporting no subscriptions. `rows_truncated: true` means the smallest counterparties were not read, so every total is a floor.

`scope` is required: `own_and_adopted` is the spend population the burn counts, `own` the workspace's own rows only.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

tools.name: well_measure_recurring_inflows
tools.title: Measure recurring inflows from bank credits
tools.description:
Measure who pays the workspace on a regular cadence, from its bank and credit card inflows: each recurring payer, its cadence, what it brings in per month, and the total per currency. It draws no card.

Call it when a cash forecast should count the inflows that keep arriving, or when the user asks which customers pay them regularly. For a forecast, pass the `forecast_inflows` entry of the forecast's currency to `well_render_cash_forecast` as `recurring_inflow`, as it is. When `forecast_inflows` holds no entry in that currency, no recurring inflow was found: draw the worst case with no `recurring_inflow` and say so.

**The server applies every rule, and the result states each one in `rules`.** Quote the figures as returned: never recompute an amount, a total or a cadence, never add a payer the person expects, and never add a one-off payment, an invoice not yet paid or a deal to the figure.

Every amount in the result is in the major units of its currency, never in cents: `1860` is 1,860.00 EUR, not 18.60 EUR.

The window is fixed: the last 24 complete calendar months in UTC and the running month. `measured_through` is the last complete month.

What the result is:
  - `recurring_inflows`: the payers on a cadence (monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, yearly), largest amount per month first, at most 50; `recurring_inflow_count` is the full count. Each carries its cadence evidence, its amount pattern (fixed, changed, varying), the amount per month, its latest month, `possibly_ended` and its category.
  - `totals`: per currency, the payer count, the amount per month of every recurring payer (a quarterly or yearly payment spread over its months), the part from payers flagged as possibly ended, and `forecast_floor_per_month`, the inflow that arrives in every month.
  - `forecast_inflows`: per currency with a positive `forecast_floor_per_month`, the `{ amount, currency, measured_through }` the cash forecast takes. It is a floor that holds month by month, so it counts only payers on a MONTHLY cadence that may not have stopped and that paid in every month of their span: every payer counts at its smallest month (the smallest amount it paid in a month of the window), never the mean. Payers on a bimonthly, quarterly or yearly cadence, and monthly payers that skipped a month (a gap of 2 in their evidence), are in `totals` and NOT in `forecast_inflows`, because they pay in some months only. A payer whose latest payment is neither in the last complete month nor in the running month is not in it either. Payers that may have stopped, payments on no cadence, possible duplicates and unattributed inflows are not in it either. Say that these were left out.
  - `not_recurring_count`, `possible_duplicate_count` and `unattributed`: what was paid in but is in no total.
  - `excluded`: what fell out, counted apart. `internal_transfers` are movements between the workspace's own accounts. `payments_from_own_accounts` are drawdowns from an owned loan, `own_company` money in from the workspace's own company, `category_excluded` the inflows whose category is a transfer, treasury, financing or tax key (`category_keys`), `unreadable_rows` rows with no readable amount or currency, `no_asset_movement` rows with no leg on an owned bank account or credit card. `scope` is required: `own_and_adopted` is the population the burn counts, `own` the workspace's own rows only. Use the scope the forecast's burn used.

tools.name: well_sum_invoices
tools.title: Sum invoices over a window
tools.description:
Sum a workspace's billed amounts over a window of whole months, grouped by month, currency and billing context. Arithmetic only — this tool holds no definition of MRR or recurrence, and returns no figure the app renders.

Use it when you are computing a figure whose RULES you are stating yourself: recurring revenue over a window you chose, a total restricted to the billing contexts a reader confirmed, a per-month series behind a trend you are about to describe. The server derives no MRR of its own, so an MRR figure starts here: state the rules, sum exactly those rows, then put the result on a card with `well_render_mrr`.

**The window is whole months.** `from` and `to` are both the first day of a month, as YYYY-MM-01; `from` is inclusive and `to` is EXCLUSIVE, so June to August is `2026-06-01` to `2026-09-01`. A bound inside a month is refused rather than widened, and so is a window longer than 36 months.

**Which rows are billed amounts is decided here, and stated so you can say it.** A draft is left out, because it has not been issued, and so is a canceled invoice. `excluded_draft_count` counts the drafts left out: a connector or document import can keep a real invoice at draft, so state the count beside any total whenever it is not zero. Only billing documents count: invoices, debit notes, credit notes and subscription billing statements, so a proforma and the invoice it precedes are not summed twice, and an order, a quote or a payment advice never is. A row with no document type is read as an invoice. Every amount is NET of tax (`items_total`), because tax collected is owed onward rather than earned.

**`party_scope` is required, and it decides whose invoice this is.** `sales` is what the workspace ISSUED — its receivables, and the only side revenue can come from. `purchase` is what it received. The two are the same rows read from opposite ends, so no default is offered: a server choosing a side would answer a different question from the one asked. `intra_self` is an invoice between two companies the workspace owns, and `unattributed` is one Well could place on neither side.

**Those four scopes partition every invoice exactly once**, which is what makes an incomplete picture visible rather than silent. `unattributed_count` comes back on every call, whatever scope you asked for: it counts the invoices in the window that landed in that fourth bucket. State it beside any total, because an unattributed invoice may still belong in the figure and nothing here can tell you whether it does.

**Every row carries ONE month, ONE currency and ONE billing context.** Currency is always a grouping key, named or not: adding EUR to USD gives a number denominated in nothing, and no field on the result would tell you it happened. Convert the per-currency subtotals yourself, at a rate you can state, before you add them.

**`totals` carries one figure per currency over the whole window**: the rows of that currency folded across months and billing contexts on the server, rounded to the cent. When your figure covers every row of the call, read it from `totals` and never add rows yourself. A figure restricted to some billing contexts, such as an MRR over the contexts a reader confirmed, still comes from the rows: `totals` folds every context in, the `null` ones too.

**`sum` is already net of credit notes.** A credit note subtracts its magnitude from its own month-currency-context bucket, whichever sign it was stored with; `credit_note_sum` and `credit_note_count` report what that removed, so you can say what the figure netted. Do not subtract them a second time. A bucket whose credit notes outweigh its invoices nets negative, and that is a real state rather than an error.

**`billing_context` is `null` on rows that name no billing arrangement** — none stored, `unknown`, or a value Well has no label for — and that is a third answer rather than a kind of one-off. The field is filled by extraction, not by a billing system, so a workspace can carry real recurring revenue on rows that say nothing about it. `unclassified_count` totals those rows. The recurring-contexts card offers them as one choice, keyed `"unclassified"`, so apply that key to these rows and only these. Counted or not, report the count rather than letting a reader read the remainder as "everything else".

`corrected_or_consolidated_count` counts the corrected and consolidated invoices among the rows. Each replaces invoices Well holds no link to, so when those originals fall in the same window the sum counts that billing twice. The rows keep them, because dropping them would lose the revenue whenever the originals fall outside the window. State the count beside any total whenever it is not zero.

`excluded_malformed` counts billing documents in the window with no readable net amount or no currency. They are in none of the rows and none of the sums, so state the count beside any total. It comes back `null` when the count could not be read, which is NOT `0`: zero says every row was readable, null says nobody counted.

When `party_scope.side_unknown` is true the workspace has no resolved own company, so no side filter was applied: the totals cover every invoice on both sides, and the side is not known. Say the side is unknown, never that the figure is the requested side's.

`partial: true` means the aggregate was cut short and every figure is a FLOOR rather than a measurement.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

tools.title: Sum outstanding receivables
tools.description:
What the workspace's customers still owe it: the outstanding receivables, one figure per currency, with the overdue part and an aging breakdown. It draws nothing.

Use it for any total of what customers owe: "who owes us money", "how much are we owed", "how much is overdue". State the totals it returns and do not add up rows yourself, and do not page `well_query_records` to rebuild a total: this read sums every outstanding invoice on the server, so the same question gives the same figure each time. For the invoices behind the figure (which customer, which invoice), read the rows with `well_show_records`.

**The rule is fixed, and `rule` echoes it.** An invoice counts as owed when the workspace is the issuer and the customer the receiver, it is a billing document (`rule.document_types`, or no type at all; never a proforma, quote, order or credit note), it is not a draft or canceled, its payment status is `unpaid` or `partial`, and `balance_due` is above zero. The amount is `balance_due`, so a part-paid invoice counts for what is left. Payment status decides, never `balance_due` alone: an invoice a connector calls settled keeps a balance until a bank payment matches it.

**Every figure is per currency and never converted.** `currencies` holds one row per currency. Do not add two rows without converting them at a rate you can state. Each row has `outstanding_count` and `outstanding_total`, the `overdue_count` and `overdue_total` part past its due date, and `aging`: the bands `current` (not yet due, or due today), `1_30`, `31_60`, `61_90` and `over_90` days past due, every band present even at zero. The bands and the invoices with no due date add up to the outstanding total.

**`as_of` is the instant of the read, and due dates are aged against `as_of_date`,** the UTC calendar date. Give `as_of` beside every figure.

**What the figure leaves out is returned so you can say it:**
- `no_due_date_count` and `no_due_date_total` (per row): outstanding invoices with no due date. They are in the outstanding total and in no aging band, and no other date stands in for a missing due date.
- `marked_paid_count` and `marked_paid_total` (per row): issued invoices a connector says are settled with no bank payment matched yet, with a balance left. They are NOT in the outstanding total. State them on their own line.
- `draft_count` and `draft_total` (per row): draft invoices with a balance left, at any payment status except `unknown`. A draft at `marked_paid` is counted here, not in the marked-paid line. An imported sales invoice often stays a draft while it is owed. They are NOT in the outstanding total. State them on their own line.
- `unsettled_credit_note_count` and `unsettled_credit_note_total` (per row): issued credit notes still unpaid or part paid with a balance left. The read does not tell a note linked to its invoice from one that is not, so say "credit notes with a balance left", never "unlinked". They are NOT in the outstanding total and are NOT subtracted from it. State them on their own line.
- `unknown_payment_status_count`: invoices, drafts included, whose payment status could not be worked out. Their balance is not trusted, so they are in no figure and in no draft line. `null` means the count failed, which is not `0`.
- `unattributed_count`: outstanding-looking invoices Well could place on neither side. They may be owed to the workspace and are in no figure. `null` means the count failed, and it is also `null` when `customer_ids` narrows the read.
- `no_currency_count`: invoices with no currency, among the outstanding ones and among the marked-paid, draft and credit-note lines. They are in no row. `null` means the count failed.
- `no_balance_count`: unpaid or part-paid invoices, drafts included, with no `balance_due` recorded, so no amount to count. In no figure. `null` means the count failed.
- `outstanding_payment_unknown_count`: invoices that ARE counted in `outstanding` and in its figure, but whose payment cannot be seen because the workspace holds no bank line within 90 days of their dates (`rule.outstanding_payment_unknown`). It is an "of which" of the outstanding count: never add it to a total, never list it as a held-back line, never subtract it from the figure. It is not `unknown_payment_status_count`: that count is a recompute that halted (balance not trusted, in no figure), while this one is counted in `outstanding` but no bank line covers the invoice's dates, so whether it was paid cannot be seen. Never say those invoices are unpaid for certain, and never say nothing is owed because no payment was matched. State it only when it is above 0: at 0 say nothing about it. `null` means the count failed.
- `party_scope`: when `party_scope.side_unknown` is true the workspace has no resolved own company, so no side filter was applied: the figures cover every invoice on both sides, and the side is not known. Say the side is unknown, never that the figure is what customers owe.
State every count beside the total, even at zero, so a reader can tell a clean read from a silent one, except `outstanding_payment_unknown_count`: it is an "of which" note, not a figure the reader asked for. Never count rows yourself to fill one in.

`customer_ids` narrows the read to those customers (company ids, at most 20). It matches each company id exactly, and one customer can exist as several company rows (aliases), so pass every company id that names the customer or the figure leaves out the invoices filed under the others. Omit it for every customer.

`partial: true` means the aggregate was cut short and every figure is a FLOOR. When `success` is false the read failed: the empty `currencies` is not a measured zero.

tools.name: well_sum_payslips
tools.title: Sum payslips
tools.description:
The payroll total of a window of whole months, summed on the server from the payslips: gross pay, net pay, employee deductions, employer charges and the payslip cost, one group per currency, and per month when `axes` holds "month". It draws nothing.

Use it for any payroll or payslip total: "what did payroll cost last month", "total employer charges this quarter", "masse salariale", "coût employeur total". State the figures it returns and never add payslip amounts yourself, and never sum payslips with `well_query_records` or a records statistic: this read applies one rule on every surface, so the same question gives the same figure. For the payslips behind a figure, read the rows with `well_show_records`.

**The window** is `from` (inclusive) to `to` (exclusive), each the first day of a month as YYYY-MM-01, at most 12 months, cut on the pay period end. One month is `from: "2026-09-01", to: "2026-10-01"`.

**The rule is fixed, and `rule` echoes it.** Statuses summed: `approved` and `paid`, and a payslip with no status, unless `statuses` names others. `employee_deductions` adds each deduction line by its magnitude; `employer_charges` adds the charge lines as printed, so a negative one is a reversal. Memo lines count nowhere. `payslip_cost` is `gross_pay + employer_charges`.

**Every figure is per currency and never converted.** Do not add two groups of different currencies.

**What the figures leave out is returned so you can say it:** `gross_unread_count` and `net_unread_count` (payslips that printed no amount there, in no total: say unread, never zero), `unclassified_line_count` and `unclassified_line_amount` (lines with no side, in no side total), `held_back` (payslips of other statuses, by status: drafts, pending, cancelled), `unplaced_count` (no pay period end, in no window) and `no_currency_count`.

**People floor.** On a WhatsApp turn each amount needs at least 3 people (distinct employment contracts) behind it: payslips that printed it for `gross_pay` and `net_pay`, deduction or charge lines for `employee_deductions` and `employer_charges`, both of those for `payslip_cost`. A person counts toward an amount only when their share of it is not zero: a payslip or line of 0.00, or none, adds no one. An amount under 3 people, or a total over several months where one month is under 3 people for it, is `null` and listed in `suppressed` as `{ amount, reason: "below_people_floor" }`. `unclassified_line_amount` is always `null` there (`reason: "not_on_whatsapp"`). State the amounts that remain and say the others show in the Well web app. On WhatsApp `payslip_count` and `contract_count` are `null` and `meets_people_floor` says whether at least 3 people of the group have a non-zero gross or net pay: never state or guess a headcount there. On WhatsApp omit `statuses`; the read refuses it there. Never rebuild a held-back amount from other reads, other amounts or other windows. There is no per-person total.

`partial: true` means part of the payroll is not in the figures, and `partial_reasons` says why: `read_cut_short` (a read was cut short and a figure may be a floor) or `currency_cap` (the window holds more than 4 currencies; `currencies_not_summed` names those in no group, so say they are left out) or `deadline` (the read ran out of time: `months_not_summed` names the months in no group, so say those months are missing and never read them as zero; a month with no group that is not listed there had no payslip to sum). When `success` is false the read failed: the empty `groups` is not a measured zero.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

tools.name: well_measure_customer_ltv
tools.title: Measure customer lifetime value
tools.description:
Measure the revenue lifetime value (LTV) of every customer the workspace invoiced over a window of whole months, with the portfolio churn and lifespan it rests on. It draws nothing.

Use it to rank customers by lifetime value, or to state what a customer is worth over its life. Do not use it for revenue in a period (`well_sum_invoices`), for recurring revenue (MRR), or for what customers still owe (receivables aging). Do not page `well_query_records` to rebuild this figure: this read covers every invoice in the window, unless `partial` is true (a month with very many customers can be cut short; see below).

**The rule is fixed, and `rule` echoes it on every call.** LTV = average order value x monthly purchase frequency x lifespan in months. It is a REVENUE LTV: no margin or cost is applied, so say "revenue lifetime value" and never present it as profit.
- Revenue: the billing documents the workspace ISSUED and did not cancel (a draft is not issued, so it is left out), net of tax (`items_total`), credit notes netted. Payment status plays no part.
- Per customer and currency: `aov` = `net_revenue` / `invoice_count`; `monthly_frequency` = `invoice_count` / `active_span_months`, where the span runs from the customer's first invoice month to the last month of the window, for every customer including a churned one. `net_revenue` is what the customer was billed over the window: give it beside the LTV.
- A churned customer's LTV: A churned customer's LTV can be lower than its billed net revenue, because its frequency counts the months after it churned, and it moves with the window end. Do not present it as what the customer was worth: net_revenue is what it was billed. State that limit when you name a churned customer's LTV (`churned: true`), and name the window end it depends on.
- Churned: no invoice for 2 x the customer's usual interval (the median gap between its invoice months), and at least 3 months. A customer invoiced in one month only takes the 3-month floor.
- Portfolio: `monthly_churn` = churned customers / `observed_customer_months`, the months customers were at risk of churning (a customer counts from its first invoice month until it churns, or until the window ends if it has not churned; a churned customer adds no month after its churn); `lifespan_months` = 1 / `monthly_churn`, capped at 60. `cap_applied: true` means the lifespan IS the cap (zero churn, or a churn so low its inverse passes the cap): state that the cap applied, and give the churned count beside it.
- A window with no invoiced customer gives `rows: []` and a null `monthly_churn` and `lifespan_months`. Say the window holds no invoiced customers. State no LTV, lifespan or churn for it, and do not call it zero churn.
- A customer flagged `young` has an active span under 12 months: its frequency is normalised per month over that short span. Say so when you name one.

**The window is whole, COMPLETE months, given one of two ways, never both.**
- By its length: `last_complete_months` (1 to 60). The server reads that many complete months, ending with the last complete month. Use it for "the last N months" and for the default window, `last_complete_months: 60`, rather than working the dates out yourself.
- By its bounds: `from` and `to`, both the first day of a month, as YYYY-MM-01; `from` is inclusive and `to` is EXCLUSIVE. Use them for a named period, such as a calendar year. The window may not reach the running month, so `to` is at most the first day of the current month, and it covers at most 60 months.
The result's `window` echoes the `from` and `to` read and `month_count`, the complete months they cover. State the window from that echo: `month_count` months, from `from` to the month before `to`.

**Amounts are never converted.** Each row is one customer in ONE currency, and `currencies` summarises each currency apart. Never add rows of two currencies without converting them first at a rate you can state. A customer billed in two currencies has two rows; converted, they add up.

**`counterparty_alias_sets` folds company rows that are one customer.** Pass the sets the own-company step confirmed, as arrays of company ids; each set folds into its first id, and `alias_company_ids` lists what was folded. Without it nothing is folded.

**The workspace's own company should be set.** Without it Well cannot tell what the workspace issued: the call still returns, but `party_scope.side_unknown` is true, no side filter was applied and the ranking covers invoices on both sides. Say the side is unknown, never that these are the customers' figures; resolve the own company, then call again for a true ranking.

**What the figure cannot reach, stated beside it:**
- `unattributed_count`: billing documents Well could place on neither side. They may belong to a customer; state the count when it is above zero. `null` means the count failed, which is not `0`.
- `excluded_draft_count`: drafts in the window. They are in no row, and a connector or document import can keep a real invoice at draft, so state the count when it is above zero. `null` means the count failed.
- `excluded_no_customer`: issued documents with no identified customer. They are in no row.
- `excluded_malformed`: issued documents with no readable net amount or no currency. `null` means the count failed.
- `credit_note_only_count`: customer and currency pairs with credit notes and no invoice in the window.
- `corrected_or_consolidated_count`: corrected or consolidated invoices among the rows, which may count billing twice with the invoices they replace.
- `omitted_row_count`: rows past the first 100 of a currency. They still count in `currencies` and `portfolio`.
- `partial: true` means a monthly read was cut short, so some customers' invoices are missing. That can move a customer's churn, the lifespan and every LTV in either direction: the figures are not bounds. Name the truncation in the reply and do not present any figure as a minimum or a maximum.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

tools.name: well_render_customer_ltv
tools.title: Render the customer lifetime value ranking
tools.description:
Draw the customer lifetime value (LTV) ranking as a bar chart card: one bar per customer, the highest first.

**Call it once, after `well_measure_customer_ltv`, and send no figure.** It runs the measure itself for the workspace of the call and draws that result, so every name, flag and LTV on the card is the server's. You pass only: `window` as the measure's result echoed it (`from`, `to` and `month_count`), `counterparty_alias_sets` exactly as you passed them to the measure, the `currency` the card draws, `left_off_currencies` and `conversions`. Read the figures for your answer from the measure's result, not from this tool's. Do not call it when the measure returned no row: say there is nothing to rank instead.

**One currency per card.** Set `currency` to the currency the card draws. Every other currency in the measure's `currencies` goes in exactly one of two places. Convert it: add a `conversions` entry with the rate into `currency` and its date, from the currency conversion step, and the tool applies it to each customer's LTV. Or leave it off: name it in `left_off_currencies`, which keeps its customers off the card, because Well has no rate for it or because converting it is not allowed. The card's own currency is never converted and never left off. A card that converts draws only when no currency on it, the card's own currency included, has more than 100 customers, because the measure cuts rows past that. Otherwise draw the card's own currency alone and name the others in `left_off_currencies`.

The card draws at most 12 customers, never a summed "other" bar, and its small form quotes the average LTV per customer. The result states `average_ltv`, `customer_count` (the customers the average covers) and `left_out_count` (customers not drawn): say how many customers the card leaves out when it is above zero.

REFUSED rather than drawn:
  - a window that reaches the running month or covers more than 60 months
  - a measured currency that is neither converted nor left off, or a currency the measure did not find
  - the card's own currency in `left_off_currencies` or in `conversions`
  - a rate more than 1% away from Well's stored rate for the pair on its rate date, a rate dated outside the window's last complete month, or two rates for one currency
  - a card that converts when the measure cut rows from a currency on it

Because the measure runs again here, a ranking reads the invoices twice. That is by design: it is what ties the card to the server's figures.

party_scope.description: What the receivable side resolved to. `side_unknown: true` means the workspace resolved no own company, so NO side filter was applied (`applied: false`) and the ranking covers invoices on both sides — say the side is unknown, never that these are the customers' figures. `null` when no read reported a scope resolution.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

tools.name: well_get_vat_summary
tools.title: Get value added tax by period
tools.description:
Read the VAT position of a workspace over a window of whole months, grouped by the date of its entries and invoices, straight from its book (VAT on posted invoices, which is the debit basis): per month, for the whole window as a CA3 by rate, and as totals with the net VAT payable. A French workspace gets that CA3; any other workspace, or a window with nothing posted, is answered from its draft entries and invoices (see below). It also lists the invoices whose lines or supplier leave the figure unreliable. It reads the book and computes nothing a reader has to trust blind: every amount is a decimal string in major units of `currency`, such as `"5000.00"` for five thousand euros, ready to state as returned. State each amount with its `currency` exactly as given. Never convert, scale or recompute one.

Use it for "what is my VAT this quarter", "how much VAT can I deduct", "is my VAT return ready" and "which invoices are hurting my VAT". Do not use it to sum invoices (`well_sum_invoices`) or to browse journal entries (`well_query_records`).

**The window is whole months.** `from` is the first day of the first month and `to` is the first day of the month AFTER the last one, both as YYYY-MM-01, so the second quarter of 2026 is `2026-04-01` to `2026-07-01`. On `basis: "posted"`, name both or neither: with neither, the call reads the current calendar quarter only: the quarter in progress, not the last four quarters and not the last complete one. On `basis: "possibilities"`, name both always: a call with neither is refused `invalid_period` with the current quarter's bounds in `error`, so the caller can ask again for them. To read any other period, work out `from` and `to` from today's date and pass both. A window shorter than one month, longer than 12 months, or with a bound inside a month returns `status: "invalid_period"` with the reason in `error`. It is refused, never widened.

**`months`** holds one row per calendar month, oldest first: `collected` (output VAT), `deductible` (input VAT, a positive magnitude), `net` (collected minus deductible, positive is payable), and `reverse_charge` (the self-assessed VAT on reverse-charge purchases, kept out of `collected` and `deductible`). `month_ended: false` marks a month still running, whose figures can still move. `unattributed_collected` and `unattributed_deductible` are VAT on lines that name no tax rate. `unmapped_rate_tax` is the signed net VAT (collected positive) on a rate the return has no slot for, such as 8.50 or 13.00. These three are in none of `collected`, `deductible` and `net`, so state them beside any total that is not zero. The monthly `collected`, `deductible` and `net` add up to the window totals.

**`ca3`** is the return by rate over the WHOLE window, built once from every entry in it, not summed from the monthly rows. `complete: false` means the ledger holds a figure the return cannot place: read `blocking_reasons` (`unattributed_collected_vat`, `unattributed_deductible_vat`, `unmapped_rate_percent`, `directionless_taxable_base`) and say so before quoting any total as final. Box numbers are deliberately absent: Well does not guess a printed CA3 box.

**`totals.net_due`** is the net VAT payable: collected minus deductible over the window, on the rates the return has a slot for (it leaves out `unattributed_*` and `unmapped_rate_tax`), with `position` as `payable`, `credit` or `nil`. A credit means the state owes the workspace, so never present it as a payment.

**The figure is on the debit basis.** It counts VAT when the invoice is posted. Entries are placed by their entry date, in the month of the date, never by their fiscal period, so an entry posted into a later return still shows in its own month and a filed return can differ from this figure; `basis_note` says so. On the receipts basis (TVA sur les encaissements), the default for services, VAT follows payments, so the amount payable can differ from this figure. The read models no VAT regime. State the basis beside the net figure, and say "the posted ledger shows X net VAT payable", never "you owe X".

**A window with nothing posted** is not refused. When the window holds no posted ledger entry that carries VAT, the call answers from the possibilities read of the same window instead: `status: "ok"`, `basis: "possibilities"`, with a `basis_note` saying that nothing is posted in the window yet, that the figures come from draft entries and invoices, and that the filed figure comes from closing the books. State that note beside the figures. It is NOT a nil return: never say no VAT is due. When that read finds nothing either, the answer is `no_vat_found`.

Pass **`basis: "possibilities"`** when the question is what VAT the current documents and in-progress book could become. The read includes the VAT-role entries in every state, plus invoice-header tax only when no live VAT-role entry exists for that invoice. The entries' state is a bookkeeping detail: `entries.validated_count` and `entries.draft_count` split `entry_count` by the books' state: read them, never state them, and never word an entry or an amount as validated, draft, « validé » or « brouillon » (a money answer has no validation step); state the number of entries from `entry_count`. It groups the evidence by calendar quarter (quarters follow the entry date of each entry and the issue date of each document, never the fiscal period, and a filed return can differ), keeps domestic purchases, purchases to check, sales and unsided documents separate, counts the documents between two other companies apart (`not_ours`), and reads a document in another currency in the read currency only when its stored accounting tax is in that currency; an unconverted other-currency document, or any document with no currency, is excluded and counted in `excluded`. A purchase is domestic when its registry country is France, or, only for a French workspace with no registry country, its stored SIREN, SIRET or French VAT number passes full validation; otherwise it stays to check. When `excluded.identity_grouping_truncated` is true, the identifier check read only part of the suppliers, so some French purchases may still sit in purchases to check: every amount stays whole, only that split is less precise, so say purchases to check may hold French suppliers. Utility bills (document type 901) count as purchase documents; expense receipts (902) and pro formas (325) remain out. Documents with no issue date are counted in `excluded.undated_count` but never placed in a quarter or amount; that count covers the whole workspace, not the window, so it is the same on every window. Replacement documents are counted but excluded from the money lines, and make the quarter `incomplete`. A quarter's `presentation` is `computed` (both sides evidenced, each by an entry or a document, with at least one ledger entry in the quarter and nothing unread: `net` and `position` are set), `evidence_only` (one side only, or documents alone), `incomplete` (unsided, other-currency, null-currency or replacement evidence, or entry VAT with no attributed or mapped rate, sits beside the figures) or `no_evidence` (the quarter is in the window but holds no VAT-role entry and no invoice VAT: it is returned with every amount, `net` and `position` null and a `note`; state it as no evidence found for that quarter, never as zero VAT and never as a nil position); `net` and `position` are null unless `computed`; `entries.unplaced` is the entry VAT that neither side carries: reverse charge is only reported, while unattributed and unmapped-rate VAT make the quarter `incomplete`; purchases to check are reported beside a computed position and never added to it, and a side without evidence (`purchase_evidence` or `sales_evidence` false) is absent, never zero. Ledger entries booked in another or an unstated accounting currency are counted in `excluded` and not summed. A window over twelve months answers `range_too_large` with the window you asked for; nothing is narrowed. Documents between two other companies (both parties known, neither one a company of this workspace) are counted in `counts.not_ours`, ordinary and replacing ones alike, and the VAT of those whose tax is stated in `currency` is in `documents.not_ours` of the quarter, which sums only the documents with a readable VAT, so a quarter's count can be larger than the documents behind its amount. `possibilities.not_ours_note` is the ready sentence for them: their count, quarter by quarter, how many of each have a readable VAT, and that VAT. Relay it as its own sentence beside the figures, in the language of the answer and with its numbers unchanged; compose none of your own, never add that VAT to a figure or put it inside the deductible sentence, and never call a quarter `incomplete` for them. A null `documents.not_ours` means none of the quarter's such documents has a VAT stated in `currency` (an unconverted other-currency document, a document with no currency, a replacement): the note then says none is readable, and no amount is ever 0.00. A document with no party at all is not one of them: it stays unsided. Documents whose side rests on an inference, not on proof (a company of this workspace on one leg, or a provider claim with no holder), are counted in `counts.estimated_side`, replacing ones included, and their VAT is in `documents.estimated` of the quarter, by kind (`purchase_domestic`, `purchase_to_check`, `sales`); it is never in `deductible`, `collected`, `net` or `position`. `possibilities.estimated_side_note` is the ready sentence for them: relay it once, as its own sentence beside the figures, in the language of the answer and with its numbers unchanged, never as proven, and compose none of your own. An inferred side alone never makes a quarter `incomplete`: a quarter that holds only such documents is `evidence_only`, while a replacement, unsided, other-currency or no-currency document still makes it `incomplete`; state the returned `presentation` unchanged. A null amount in `documents.estimated` means none is stated, never 0.00. Possibilities carry no `months`, `ca3` or `totals`. With no accounting country, purchases remain `to check` and no jurisdiction is inferred, unless `estimated_country_code` is set (see below). With no configured or country currency, the mode of eligible non-null document currencies is used, ties break alphabetically, and no eligible currency returns `no_vat_found`; existing ledger amounts are never relabelled. `currency_basis` says what `currency` rests on: `settings` (the workspace's books currency), `country` (the default currency of its accounting country) or `documents_mode` (the most common currency of its invoices, because neither is set); it is null, beside no `currency`, when no denomination exists. Name it only when it is not `settings`. `status: "no_vat_found"` means neither VAT-role entries nor document evidence were found in any quarter of the window (the quarters it looked at come back as `no_evidence` rows), or no denomination can be selected; it is not a nil return.

**`anomalies`** lists invoices in the window, purchases and sales, that carry a billed line with no VAT rate (`line_without_vat_rate`). A purchase that names no supplier company also lists as `supplier_unattributed`; a sale never does. `direction` says which side an invoice is on, from the workspace's own company: a `purchase` names a `supplier`, `sales` names a `customer`, and `label` uses that party. `unanchored` means the invoice does not name the own company on exactly one side, so it has no direction and no party. `total` counts every such invoice, `items` holds the first `anomaly_limit` (default 20, at most 50), and `truncated: true` means more exist than `items` shows. Name an invoice by its `label`, never by `invoice_id`. An invoice with no rate is not necessarily missing VAT: the fix is to set the rate or supplier on the invoice, not to adjust the return.

**A workspace outside France, or with no accounting country,** is not refused either. It is answered from the possibilities read, with `filing: null` (no CA3, no CA3 slots) and a `basis_note` that names the gap: VAT filing for its country is not mapped in Well, or the workspace has no accounting country, and the figures are the VAT the books and invoices carry. State that note beside the figures. With no configured country, `estimated_country_code` is the majority registry country of the workspace's own documents, an estimate stated as one: the domestic split and the French-identifier check run on it, and `basis_note` / `estimated_country` says so. `country_code` stays null: nothing configured is asserted. `estimated_country_truncated` is true when more of its documents would vote than the estimate reads, so only the newest voted, and `basis_note` then says the country leads among the newest documents read, never a majority of all of them. The estimate reads the twelve months up to today, whatever window the call names. When no country emerges, the read infers no jurisdiction and places purchases in `to check`.

**`filing`** is the VAT return Well's obligation table assigns to the workspace's own company, from its accounting country and legal form, or null when the table assigns none (the legal form is not set, or the country is not covered). `cadence` is the table's cadence for that form, which assumes the normal real regime (régime réel normal). Well stores no VAT regime and no deadline: `due_rule` is the published rule, with the `source` to name beside any date, and `due_window` is the window that rule gives for THIS read's period, the days of the month after it. It is null unless the read covers exactly one calendar month or one calendar quarter. State a date only after the person has confirmed they file on that cadence, and name the source with it.

**`scope`.** Omit it, or pass `"this_workspace"`, to read the workspace the call runs in. Pass `"my_companies"` on WhatsApp to read every company workspace of the person's company family in one call, without moving the chat: the family is the membership the chat runs in, or the company's parent membership, and its company workspaces. A workspace counts only when the signed-in person holds a live membership in it, checked again before each read, and Well finds them from the signed-in person: a workspace is never named in the call. The result then carries `workspaces`, one block per company workspace (at most 10, `workspaces_truncated: true` when more exist), each with its `workspace_name`, `company_name` and the same fields as a single read, its own `status` first. Answer each block on its own: never add, net or compare two blocks into one figure. A block for a workspace outside France or without a country answers like any other and carries its own `basis_note`; state it with that block. `workspaces_unreadable` counts the company workspaces a failed lookup left out unnamed: their position is unknown, not nil. An empty `workspaces` with `workspaces_unreadable` at 0 means the person has no company workspace they can read; with it above 0 it means the read failed. On any other host the read refuses the scope with `status: "failed"`: read one company per call there.

`status: "range_too_large"` means the window holds more posted entries than one call reads (5000). Ask again with a shorter window. It is never answered with a partial sum. `status: "failed"` means the read failed and the position is UNKNOWN, not nil.

**Unread invoice-header VAT.** On the possibilities basis, `excluded.header_tax_unread_count` counts live eligible invoices with no header tax where both item and grand totals are present and differ. It is a count of VAT the header cannot read, not an amount. `excluded.tax_unknown_count` (present when above 0) counts every live eligible invoice in the window with no header tax, whatever its totals say (`tax_unknown_split` gives the equal, missing and differing totals; the differing ones are `header_tax_unread_count`). When it is present, the answer says once how many invoices in the window have VAT that could not be read, as a count for the window as a whole: never inside a quarter, never as nil, zero or no VAT, never as an amount, and never added to another count.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

basis.description: Evidence basis. Omit or use `posted` for the existing posted-ledger VAT return; use `possibilities` for draft, posted and document-header evidence grouped by quarter.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window: the first day of a month, YYYY-MM-01. Give it with `to`, or omit both only to read the current quarter in progress on `basis: "posted"` (a `basis: "possibilities"` call always names both); for any other period name both.

to.description: EXCLUSIVE end of the window: the first day of the month after the last one you want, YYYY-MM-01. Give it with `from`.

anomaly_limit.description: How many anomalous invoices to list, at most 50. Defaults to 20; `anomalies.total` counts all of them.

scope.description: Which workspaces the read covers. Omit it for the workspace the call runs in. "my_companies" reads every company workspace of the person's family, one block each, and runs on WhatsApp only.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

tools.name: well_list_tax_deadlines
tools.title: List tax deadlines
tools.description:
List a French company's upcoming tax deadlines, computed from its tax profile: the VAT returns (CA3 monthly or quarterly, or the annual CA12 with its July and December instalments), the corporate income tax instalments, balance and return, the CFE, and the filing of the annual accounts. Use it for "what are my next tax deadlines", "quelles sont mes prochaines échéances fiscales", "when is my corporate tax due", "when do I file my accounts". It reads the profile Well holds and computes the dates; it reads no tax site and stores nothing. For the VAT amount of a period, call `well_get_vat_summary` as well.

**`deadlines`** lists the deadlines due from today for `months` months (default 3, at most 12), soonest first. Each has `due.from` and `due.to` (one day when equal; a VAT window such as the 15th to the 24th otherwise, where the administration sets the exact day per company), the `period` it covers when it covers one, a `condition` when the profile cannot settle whether it applies (`prior_year_tax_above_3000_eur`: no instalment when last year's corporate tax was under 3,000 EUR; `not_the_creation_year`: no CFE in the year of creation; `approval_on_last_allowed_day`: the latest filing day when the accounts are approved on the last day the law allows), and its `source`. State every date with its source and its condition. Never state a date that is not in `deadlines`.

**`undated`** lists the deadlines Well cannot date, each with a `reason`. `missing_profile_key`: the `missing` profile keys (`legal_form`, `vat_regime`, `vat_filing_frequency`, `corporate_tax_regime`, `fiscal_year_end`) are not set; say which are missing and ask the person, and save an answer with `well_upsert_accounting_settings`. Never guess a missing key. `unsupported_legal_form`: the legal form is set, but Well's table holds no rule for it, and `missing` is empty; say Well does not date the deadlines of that legal form, and ask nothing. **`not_owed`** lists the deadlines the profile says the company does not owe, such as the CA3 under the VAT franchise.

`status: "unsupported_jurisdiction"` means the workspace's accounting country is not France: Well holds no calendar for it. `status: "failed"` means the read failed: the calendar is unknown, never empty.

tools.name: well_prepare_vat_return
tools.title: Prepare the value added tax return
tools.description:
Prepare a French company's VAT return (CA3) for one period from its posted ledger, as a filled PDF stored in the workspace. Well prepares the return; the company files it on impots.gouv.fr. Nothing is filed, sent or paid. The PDF is the input of the `fill-ca3` browser skill, which types it into the online form and hands the form over before submit.

Call it when the person asks to prepare or file their VAT return, after the VAT position of the period was read with `well_get_vat_summary`. Pass no window for the last period that has ended (the previous month for a monthly filer, the previous quarter for a quarterly one), or `from` and `to` (YYYY-MM-01, `to` exclusive) for one named period.

The period follows the company's filing frequency from its tax profile:
- `status: "frequency_unknown"`: the profile holds no filing frequency. Ask once whether the company files every month or every quarter, save the answer with `well_upsert_accounting_settings`, and call again. Never assume one.
- `no_vat_return`: the company is in the VAT franchise and files no VAT return. `annual_return`: it files one annual CA12, which Well does not prepare.
- `period_not_ended`: a month of the window is still running. Well prepares no return before its period ends.
- `not_return_periods` or `invalid_window`: the window is not whole return periods of the company's frequency.
- `several_returns`: the window holds several periods. `periods` lists them: one return per period, so prepare each with its own call.

Then the figures, read the same way as `well_get_vat_summary`:
- `not_fileable`: the ledger holds a figure the return cannot place, listed in `reasons` (`unattributed_collected_vat`, `unattributed_deductible_vat`, `unmapped_rate_percent`, `directionless_taxable_base`, `reverse_charge_present`, `negative_line`). No PDF is printed: say why and stop.
- `no_posted_entries`: the period holds no posted VAT entry. This is not a nil return: no PDF is printed.
- `unsupported_jurisdiction` (not France), `unsupported_currency` (the books are not kept in EUR), `range_too_large`, `failed`: no PDF.

On `ok`: `document_id` names the PDF, the value of the `document` input of the `fill-ca3` skill. `lines` lists every filled box by its printed line code and column, in whole euros. `vat_due` (line TD) or `vat_credit` (line 25) is the result. `checks` lists what the person checks before filing: say each one. Never say the return is filed.

tools.name: well_get_pennylane_statements
tools.title: Build the profit and loss and balance sheet from the ledger
tools.description:
Build a profit and loss (compte de résultat) and a balance sheet (bilan) from the trial balance of the workspace's connected Pennylane. Pennylane shares no ready profit and loss or balance sheet, only its trial balance (`getTrialBalance`). Well reads every page of it and computes the totals itself, account class by account class of the French chart of accounts (PCG). Every amount is a decimal string in euros, such as `"5000.00"`. State each amount exactly as returned and name the source: "computed by Well from the Pennylane trial balance". Never add, round or recompute an amount, and never call `getTrialBalance` yourself to rebuild one.

Use it when the user asks for a profit and loss, an income statement, a compte de résultat, a balance sheet or a bilan, and the workspace's accounting tool is Pennylane. Do not use it for QuickBooks or Xero, whose own reports `well_invoke_connector_tool` reads.

**Inputs.** `workspace_connector_id` is the Pennylane accounting row's id from `well_get_connector_coverage`. `statements` is `income_statement`, `balance_sheet` or `both`. `to` is the last day, YYYY-MM-DD, never after today: the profit and loss ends on it and the balance sheet is dated on it. `from` is the first day of the profit and loss, required for `income_statement` and `both`. The period must sit inside one Pennylane fiscal year.

**Output.** `income_statement` gives `revenue` (class 7) and `expenses` (class 6), each with its `total` and its two-digit PCG `groups`, and `net_result` (revenue minus expenses, negative is a loss). `balance_sheet` gives `assets` and `equity_and_liabilities`, each with its `total` and `sections`, and `result_for_the_year` (from the fiscal year start to `to`, inside equity). The two totals are equal. `source` names the connection, the tool, the chart and each trial balance read with its dates and row count. `opening_balances` says how the balance sheet was shown to include the opening balances: carried from the closed previous year, or an opening entry on the first day of the fiscal year. `fiscal_year.status` is the year's status in Pennylane: `open` or `reopen` means entries can still be booked in it, so the figures can still change; say so once.

**Refusals carry no statement.** `opening_balances_unverified`: Well cannot show that the balance sheet includes the opening balances (à-nouveaux) of the fiscal year, usually because the previous year is not closed in Pennylane yet or its opening entry is not imported yet; the profit and loss alone still works. `trial_balance_semantics_unproven`: Well cannot show that Pennylane's trial balance holds only the movements of the dates asked for. Before every profit and loss and every balance sheet, Well splits the trial balance at one day (the day before `from` for a profit and loss that starts after the fiscal year start, otherwise the day before `to`) and checks that the two parts add up to the whole on every class 6 and 7 account. The check failed, or a statement dated on the first day of the fiscal year left no day to split at. Well then builds neither statement, and the refusal carries `trial_balance`: Pennylane's trial balance for the dates asked for, with its full `row_count` and at most its first twenty rows, each exactly as Pennylane returned it. `closing_entries_suspected`: either every profit and loss account nets to zero on `to` although the earlier days of the year moved some, or the result of the year (chapter 12) moves on `to` (checked on the last day of the span, and on the last day of the fiscal year for a later period), which means Pennylane probably booked the closing entries of the fiscal year on that day; Well builds no statement and the refusal carries `trial_balance` the same way. Show those rows as Pennylane's trial balance, never as a profit and loss or a balance sheet, and add nothing up; when `row_count` is above the rows returned, say the full trial balance is in Pennylane. `connection_not_found`: no Pennylane connection matches `workspace_connector_id` in this workspace. `unsupported_source`: the connection is not a Pennylane input connection served over MCP (`pennylane` or `pennylane-token`). `unsupported_currency`: the workspace's base currency is not EUR. `unsupported_framework`: the Pennylane company does not use a French chart of accounts. `framework_not_reviewed`: the company uses a French sector chart (agriculture, non-profit or notary) that Well's statements do not cover yet. `scope_missing`: the connection was not granted the trial balance; it needs a reconnect. `tool_not_read_only`: Well's record of the connection does not mark a Pennylane read as read-only, so Well calls nothing. `connection_not_readable`: the connection is not enabled, or its grant expired during the read (`connection_status` says which state). When the connection is in the state `need_reconnect` or `error`, a `scope_missing` or `connection_not_readable` refusal carries `reconnect_url`, the link that reconnects this Pennylane connection: give it to the user as a clickable link, exactly as returned, and never build a connector link yourself. Without `reconnect_url`, give no link. `read_incomplete`: the trial balance did not come back whole. `invalid_trial_balance`: the trial balance came back whole but does not balance or holds a row Well cannot read (`defect` says which). `fiscal_year_not_found` and `invalid_period`: the dates do not fit one Pennylane fiscal year. `failed`: the read failed and nothing is known. Say each refusal in one plain line and state no figure, except the `trial_balance` rows of `trial_balance_semantics_unproven` and `closing_entries_suspected`, shown as returned.

tools.name: well_render_mrr
tools.title: Render a caller-computed recurring revenue figure
tools.description:
Put an MRR figure YOU computed onto the MRR card.

**This tool measures nothing.** It takes the figure and its method as input and returns them for rendering. Call it only after you have computed the recurring revenue yourself and can state every field below from your own work — never to "get" an MRR.

The server derives no MRR of its own. The figure on the card is the one you state here, which is why every field below is required: the policy behind a number is the only thing that makes it checkable.

**At its smallest size the card draws the figure alone.** It carries the figure, the window it averages and the trend chip. At its wider sizes it draws a donut of `by_context` when you send it, and the donut labels each slice from its key. The recurring contexts reach the card only through that split; they are not drawn as a list. Everything else you state below is REQUIRED and is not drawn. All of it comes back in this tool's text result, which is what you write the prose from. The card is the measure; the explanation is yours.

OPTIONAL, and sent whenever you can state it:
  - `by_context` — the same average split by billing context: one entry per key in `recurring_contexts`, each `{ key, amount }`, where `amount` is that context's own monthly average over the same window, the same divisor and the same conversion as `amount`. Send EVERY recurring context, the largest first, and do not group any of them yourself: the server keeps the 4 largest by name and folds the rest, and every slice under 1.5% of the total, into one "Other" slice. Send no label and no share. The server names each context from its key and derives each share from the amounts, and returns both. When a context nets negative over the window, send no `by_context` at all: a split cannot draw a negative slice, and the figure still renders alone.

REQUIRED, because a figure whose method is not stated cannot be checked:
  - `amount` — the recurring revenue per month in `currency`, net of tax and of credit notes, as the sum returned it
  - `window` — the months the average divides by, not the months that carried revenue
  - `months_in_window` and `months_with_revenue` — a window with dark months reports LOWER than its typical month. When the two differ you MUST say so in prose: how many months recorded recurring revenue, and that the average still divides by the whole window
  - `recurring_contexts` — the billing contexts the reader confirmed as recurring, as the keys the card recorded. `"unclassified"` among them means the reader counted the invoices with no billing context (the sum rows whose `billing_context` is `null`) as recurring. This is the reader's half of the policy. The card names a few of them at most, and none at its smallest size, so an answer that does not name them leaves the figure unchecked
  - `invoice_count`, `unattributed_count` and `unclassified_count` — how much of the window the figure could reach at all. `invoice_count` is the issued invoices; `unattributed_count` is the SEPARATE set Well could place on neither side, reported beside it rather than inside it, and it may be larger. An unattributed invoice may still be recurring revenue. An unclassified one carries no billing context: it is in the figure only when `recurring_contexts` holds `"unclassified"`, and when it is, say in prose that the reader chose to count it. Send `null` for a count the sum returned as `null`: it is unmeasured, not zero
  - `excluded` — what fell out, as three invoice COUNTS kept apart: `one_off` (issued invoices under a context the reader did not count), `credit_notes` (the `credit_note_count` netted into the figure) and `unreadable_rows` (the sum's `excluded_malformed`, `null` when unmeasured)

REFUSED rather than rendered, each because your own figures disagree with each other:
  - a negative `amount` — the credit notes outweighed the recurring invoices, so net recurring revenue fell below zero. That is a finding to report in prose, not a figure to put on a card, and never one to flip to its magnitude
  - an empty `recurring_contexts` — an MRR with nothing counted as recurring is not an MRR of zero, it is a policy nobody stated. Say the figure has nothing to measure instead
  - `months_with_revenue` above `months_in_window`, or `unclassified_count` above `invoice_count`
  - a `months_in_window` that disagrees with the months `window` spans — the two state one fact
